objective: Acquire and container-verify the exact 10 August before and 26 August early-after Landsat-9 Collection 2 Level-2 full product bundles from the owner-signed-in USGS EarthExplorer session into non-Git custody, so a separately reviewed Landsat pixel and map route can be evaluated.

single_owner_decision_requested.approval_effect: One conditional envelope from control integration and synthetic tests through sanitized terminal publication; no intermediate owner reconfirmation while source identity, browser host, rights, scope, and attempt bounds remain unchanged.
allowed_actions_in_dependency_order: Implement the browser-completed-download to unique external staging handoff and synthetic secret-exposure, interruption, collision, container-identity, and no-replace tests; keep all real account material outside code and records.

Integrate only the exact two planned assets and current source gate into project controls; publish source-safe code, controls, tests, and review evidence to the public default branch and require passing public CI before any real request.

Run a final no-payload preflight of source IDs, rights and account-condition drift, browser signed-in state and exact full-bundle buttons, local paths, free space, collision absence, and durable receipt reservations.

After every gate passes, initiate a controlled browser download of the exact before full product bundle, then the exact early-after full product bundle; capture completion paths without persisting signed URLs, cookies, tokens, or account identifiers.

For each completed bundle, preserve actual file length and SHA-256, copy into unique external staging, run the reviewed TAR/MTL container verifier, and conditionally promote only passing bytes by atomic no-replace operation; reconcile terminal and cleanup evidence.
Publish sanitized terminal receipts and exact post-CI reconciliation without placing product bytes, imagery, account data, signed URLs, or local private paths into Git.
single_owner_decision_requested.request_budget: At most one initial owner-initiated full-bundle download per exact product, plus at most one distinct fresh byte-zero recovery per same product after a clearly classified transport or local persistence failure, unchanged source/terms verification, preserved terminal evidence, and no promoted destination. No automatic loops or second request after a content-identity, rights, security, or unexplained verification failure.
stop_on: A different product, host, bundle type, account condition, legal term, or paid/download restriction appears.
The browser cannot expose a completed local file or the handoff cannot keep account material out of receipts and process arguments.
The first bundle fails an unresolved source, container, or custody check; do not proceed to the second until the first is verified or the bounded recovery passes.
A shared credential, storage, path-containment, security, or no-replace guarantee fails.

frozen_checks.transport: EarthExplorer Product Options / Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 Product Bundle only; no band-group Download All Files Now, bulk queue, M2M API, Microsoft Planetary Computer, or other host.
frozen_checks.container: Safe uncompressed TAR, all members streamed, required MTL.txt/XML and QA/SR member identities present and nonempty, exact scene and product IDs in both MTL forms, local hashes and lengths, no unsafe paths/types, duplicates, trailing payload, or partial promotion.
frozen_checks.provider_identity_limit: The EarthExplorer display size is rounded and no upstream digest or exact byte length was observed; local SHA-256 and MTL identity establish local custody and structural consistency, not cryptographic equivalence to an unpublished upstream digest.

explicit_exclusions: No source substitution, M2M token, credential storage or exposure, account or terms acceptance, paid credits, or unbounded retry.
No TIFF header or pixel read, AOI cloud/snow/terrain mask, registration, index, baseline admission, change analysis, interpretation, or attribution.
No ArcGIS raster map, derived-pixel publication, scientific publication, or claim that a product bundle proves usable imagery or event effects.
